ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in Figure 8, a metal cup containing cold water is placed on the upper end of the coil. After the AC power supply is connected, after a few minutes the water in the cup boils. If the above heating time is to be shortened, what measure can be taken by changing the coil?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Increase the number of turns of the coil
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left side of the figure is labeled “AC power supply,” and the two ends of the power supply are connected to a coil wound around the outside of a vertical iron core; the right side is labeled “iron core.” A metal cup containing water is placed near the upper ends of the coil and the iron core, and the water in the cup is represented with dashed lines. Reasoning: After the AC power supply is connected, the alternating current in the coil produces a changing magnetic field, and the changing magnetic field causes induced eddy currents to be produced in the metal cup; the eddy currents generate heat, causing the water temperature to rise and boil. The question restricts that the heating time should be shortened by “changing the coil,” so the coil should be made to produce a stronger changing magnetic field, thereby increasing the induced eddy currents and heating power in the metal cup. A feasible measure for changing the coil is to increase the number of turns of the coil.
